ex001.name: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
ex001.instructions:
Set the bench to a low incline (30 degrees). Lie back and pinch your shoulder blades together so your chest sticks out. When you lower the weights, tuck your elbows in at a 45-degree angle (like an arrow), don't flare them out wide (like a T). Lower the weights until they touch your outer chest, then press up. Stop just before your elbows lock out to keep the tension on your chest.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.

ex002.name: Leg Extension
ex002.instructions:
Sit in the machine and adjust the pad so it sits right on your ankles/shins. Hold the handles tight to keep your butt in the seat. Kick your legs up until they are straight and squeeze your quads hard at the top. Lower the weight slowly—don't let the stack slam down.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.

ex003.name: Pull Up
ex003.instructions: Grab the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width. initiate the movement by driving your elbows down toward your ribs, not by pulling with your biceps. pulling your chest all the way to the bar.
ex003.notes: Best back width builder (or Lat Pulldown)

ex004.name: Cable Lateral Raise
ex004.instructions:
Set the cable pulley to the very bottom. Stand sideways to the machine. Grab the handle with the hand furthest away from the machine. Step out so the weight stack is lifted slightly even when your arm is down. Lift your arm out to the side, leading with your elbow, not your hand. Think about pushing your knuckles toward the wall, not the ceiling. Stop when your arm is parallel to the floor.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex004.notes: CRITICAL: Creates shoulder width and V-taper

ex005.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
ex005.instructions:
Sit with the bench almost vertical (about 75 degrees) so you have back support. Kick the weights up to your shoulders. Press straight up overhead until your arms are straight. On the way down, control the weight all the way until the dumbbells actually touch your shoulders. Don't stop at ear level—that’s a half rep. Keep your core tight so you don't arch your lower back too much.

This is a multiplier 2 lift: if you have 50 lb in either hand/arm/side, log 50 lb total.

ex006.name: Back Squat
ex006.instructions:
Put the bar on your traps (not your neck). Step back, set your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out. Take a huge breath into your stomach and brace your abs. Break at the hips and knees at the same time. Sit down until the crease of your hip is below the top of your knee. Drive back up through the middle of your foot. Keep your knees pushed out; don't let them cave in.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.

ex007.name: Standing Machine Calf Press
ex007.instructions:
Put the balls of your feet on the edge of the platform. Lower your heels as far down as physically possible—this stretch is the most important part. Pause for a second at the bottom. Then push up onto your big toes. Don't bounce.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex007.notes: Full stretch at bottom, pause at top

ex008.name: Seated Leg Curl
ex008.instructions:
Sit in the machine and clamp the thigh pad down tight so your legs can't move. Kick your legs down and back under you. Squeeze at the bottom. Control the weight on the way up. Don't use momentum to jerk the weight down.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.

ex009.name: Cable Crunch
ex009.instructions:
Use the rope attachment on a high pulley. Kneel down facing the machine. Hold the rope next to your ears. Crunch down by aiming your forehead toward your knees. Visualize curling your spine like a shrimp. Don't just bend at the hips—your back *should* round on this one to contract the abs. Exhale all your air as you crunch down.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.

ex012.name: Lat Pulldown
ex012.instructions:

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.

ex014.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
ex014.instructions:

Set the cable pulley to about waist height (or lower). Grab the rope, turn away from the machine, and press the rope overhead. Your elbows should stay pointing at the ceiling the whole time. Only your forearms move. Lower the rope behind your head until you feel a deep stretch in your triceps, then extend your arms straight up. Flare your hands out at the top.

ex025.name: Romanian Deadlift
ex025.instructions:
Hold a barbell or dumbbells standing tall. Keep your legs slightly bent (soft knees), but lock them in that position—your knees shouldn't bend any more than that. Push your hips backward like you are trying to close a car door with your butt. Keep the weight sliding down your thighs. Go down until you feel a massive stretch in your hamstrings (usually mid-shin). Squeeze your glutes to stand back up. Keep your back flat the entire time.

ex357.name: Single-arm Cable Row
ex357.instructions:
sit down on the seated machine (or stand if necessary) and row your elbow back toward your hip, letting your torso rotate slightly into the stretch at the front. Pause and squeeze your lat, then control the handle back out without letting the stack slam.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex357.notes: Constant-tension lat row with a big stretch

ex358.name: Standing Multi Flight
ex358.instructions:
Adjust both arms to match the movement you want: forward for rear delts, open and slightly behind you for chest fly, or lower for lateral raises. Set the chest pad so your torso stays supported and your shoulders line up with the handles. Keep a small bend in your elbows and move in a wide arc instead of turning it into a press or row. Pause for a clean squeeze, then control the handles back without letting the stack slam.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex358.notes: Multi-use fly machine. Use the arm position to choose chest fly, rear delt fly, or lateral raise.

ex359.name: Hammer Strength Lateral Raise
ex359.instructions:
Sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad and your upper arms under the roller pads. Keep your shoulders down and your elbows slightly bent. Raise your elbows out to the sides until your upper arms are about parallel with the floor. Lead with the elbows, not the hands, and avoid shrugging. Lower slowly until the stack almost touches.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex359.notes: Machine lateral raise. Great for controlled side delt work without needing to stabilize dumbbells.

ex360.name: MegaMass Leverage Chest Press
ex360.instructions:
Adjust the seat so the handles start around mid-chest, then sit tall with your back pinned to the pad. Pull your shoulder blades back and down before you start. Press the handles forward in a smooth arc, keeping your elbows a little below shoulder height instead of flared straight out. Stop just short of locking out, squeeze your chest, then lower under control until you feel a stretch across your pecs.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex360.notes: Plate-loaded leverage chest press with independent arms. Use controlled reps and match loading on both sides.

ex361.name: Machine Pullover
ex361.instructions:
Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot point and the pad or handles sit against your upper arms. Keep your chest against the pad and your ribs down. Drive your elbows down and back in an arc until your upper arms are near your sides. Squeeze your lats at the bottom, then let the handles come back up slowly until you feel a stretch without letting the weight stack slam.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex361.notes: Machine lat isolation. Keep the movement at the shoulders instead of turning it into a triceps pressdown.

ex362.name: Cable Rear Delt Crossover
ex362.instructions:
Set both cable pulleys around shoulder height and remove the handles if the cable ends are easier to grip. Grab the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand so your arms cross in front of you. Step back, keep a soft bend in your elbows, and pull your hands apart until your arms are out to your sides. Squeeze the back of your shoulders, then return slowly without letting the weight pull your shoulders forward.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex362.notes: Rear delt cable fly variation with constant tension. Use light weight and control the stretch.

ex363.name: Preacher Curl Machine
ex363.instructions:
Adjust the seat so your upper arms rest flat on the preacher pad and your armpits are close to the top edge. Grab the handles with your wrists straight. Curl the handles up by bending your elbows, squeeze your biceps at the top, then lower slowly until your arms are almost straight. Keep your chest against the pad and do not lift your elbows off the support.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex363.notes: Wrist-friendly machine curl that makes cheating hard. Avoid fully relaxing at the bottom.

ex364.name: Seated Dumbbell Shrug
ex364.instructions:
Sit tall on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand and your arms hanging straight at your sides. Keep your chest up and your neck neutral. Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause briefly at the top, then lower under control until you feel your traps stretch. Do not roll your shoulders forward or backward.

This is a multiplier 2 lift: if you have 50 lb in either hand/arm/side, log 50 lb total.
ex364.notes: Seated version of dumbbell shrugs. Removes leg drive and keeps the movement strict.

ex365.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
ex365.instructions:
Sit in the leg press and place the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform with your heels hanging off. Keep a slight bend in your knees and unlock the safety handles. Let your heels drop slowly until you feel a calf stretch, then press through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as possible. Pause at the top, then lower under control. Keep the sled stable and do not bounce out of the bottom.

This is a multiplier 1 lift: if you put 50 lb on either side, log 100 lb total.
ex365.notes: Calf raise performed on the leg press. Use the safeties and keep the range controlled.
